title: The Tuxedo
full_review:
"The Tuxedo" (DreamWorks) is a James-Bond-wannabe action comedy in which James Bond is James Tong (Jackie Chan), a mild-mannered cabbie-turned-secret-agent. Once Tong dons a specially customized tuxedo he can leap, run, kick and slug with abandon, sure to please every Chan fan -- but what about the rest of us?

These frequent fisticuffs usually include Tong's rookie agent partner (Jennifer Love Hewitt) punching and kickboxing by his side while predictably acting hostile toward him -- even though you know she won't be able to resist his puppy-dog expressions for long. But long is the operative word here. With a feeble story in the background (megalomaniac seeks global domination by controlling the world's water supply) the silly proceedings soon play like a drawn-out fantasy -- but they would have played better at half-hour sitcom length.

Aside from that, novice director Kevin Donovan turns in workmanlike visuals and orchestrates the fight scenes to be more comic than violent. Yet an early scene in which another agent is drowned initially gives the film a nasty edge, but once Chan shows up the action is mostly innocuous if not involving.

A scene in which Tong doesn't realize his own strength and accidentally KOs soul legend James Brown (playing himself) draws chuckles when Tong goes on stage as his replacement. Soon after, the airhead girlfriend (Mia Cottet) of the villain (Ritchie Coster) tries to seduce Tong but he is too busy fighting off the interchangeable goons who populate the picture as punching bags for the two hyperactive agents.

Subsequent scenes where the twosome discover the villain's underground lab are cut-rate versions of Bond movies -- with similarly cut-rate excitement.

Because of brief deadly violence, much comic violence and some sexual innuendo, the U.S. Conference of Catholic Bishops classification is A-II -- adults and adolescents. The Motion Picture Association of America rating is PG-13 -- parents are strongly cautioned. Some material may be inappropriate for children under 13.
